_why: PLA-8 batch 25 (herbs). TARGET STATE, pinned before fan-out. Decided against the live roster from the seven record/source reports plus Trevor's four structural rulings (2026-09-04): retire both non-problems, split all four bundles, drop lavender's aphid half, oregano names become 'Mint rust' + 'Powdery mildew'. `from` records provenance so the promote can be verified against canonical.
_counts: 36 canonical problems -> 38 target (2 retired, 4 bundles split into 9, 1 half deleted).

pests.name: Spittlebug
pests.evidence: No spittlebug id exists anywhere on the roster; this batch mints the family. Philaenus spumarius, per rhs which names the binomial and lists 'lavender, rosemary' in one host sentence. Shared with rosemary and sage.

pests.name: Whiteflies
pests.from: RENAME from 'Whiteflies and aphids' (aphid half DELETED, Trevor 2026-09-04)
pests.evidence: `whiteflies` live on 5 crops. Aphid half unsupported across 8 documents; UC IPM's lavender host-index omits aphids while its rosemary page lists them, so the omission reads deliberate.

diseases.name: Phytophthora root and crown rot
diseases.evidence: THE EXCEPTION to the rot-family rule, and the only one: taxon RESOLVED and NARROWER than the umbrella (Phytophthora, P. nicotianae per Putnam 1991 via the dedicated admitted source wsu_ext_lavender_prcr), and the display name already names the genus. Distinct from `phytophthora-root-rot` (blueberry/raspberry/blackberry), a different Phytophthora on a different host family.

diseases.name: Leaf spot
diseases.evidence: PLA-448 4f RULING: umbrella, NOT one unpinned organism. US extension names exactly one organism on Lavandula (Septoria lavandulae, ncsu newcropsorganics) in a bulk list with no symptoms, distribution or management; ncsu toolbox itself says only 'susceptible to leaf spot and root rot'. Do NOT reuse `leaf-spots` (marigold's bundles powdery mildew).

pests.name: Spider mites (indoor and hot, dry conditions)
pests.evidence: `spider-mites` live on 16 crops. Type corrected from coarse `pest` to `mite`: zero of 823 laddered entries carry coarse types.

diseases.name: Lemongrass rust
diseases.evidence: Puccinia nakanishikii Dietel, per CTAHR PD-57 read in full. PD-57 prints the host range as Cymbopogon only, so the Poaceae/Lamiaceae separation from mint-rust and oregano-rust is on evidence, not assumption.

diseases.name: Leaf blight
diseases.evidence: usu_ext genuinely lists it ('Reddish brown spots on leaf tips and margins'). Organism JOURNAL-ONLY (four reports, all Curvularia, four different species) so the id stays host-scoped and taxon-neutral. NAME_SHARED with carrot-leaf-blight is a parenthetical-deletion artifact; register.

diseases.name: Root rot (overwatering in poor drainage)
diseases.evidence: Neither cited source names an organism. Monocot grass, so not the Lamiaceae rots; the existing 6-crop umbrella is the roster's problem-class id for exactly this shape and all 6 ladder improve_drainage-first.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.evidence: 59 crops. type/severity were ABSENT keys on all 6 mint problems; supplied.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.evidence: 16 crops; roster convention `mite` (30/34).

pests.name: Cutworms
pests.from: SPLIT 1/3 from 'Cutworms, mint flea beetles, and root-feeding pests'
pests.evidence: 9 crops. usu_ext: 'Larvae feed at or below ground and sever stems of seedlings or plants.'

pests.name: Flea beetles
pests.from: SPLIT 2/3 from 'Cutworms, mint flea beetles, and root-feeding pests'
pests.evidence: 34 crops. DE-NAMED from 'mint flea beetles': usu_ext writes only 'Flea Beetle' with no species, and Longitarsus waterhousei appears on NO catalog-admitted document. On a home patch the beetle seen is more likely a drifting Epitrix or Phyllotreta.

pests.name: Mint root borer
pests.from: SPLIT 3/3 from 'Cutworms, mint flea beetles, and root-feeding pests'
pests.evidence: Fumibotys fumalis, per uc_ipm mint-root-borer (ANR 3457). The record's root-feeder limb was cited to nothing; this page carries it. NOTE: this is a UC IPM AGRICULTURE page, so its per-acre nematode rate and postharvest threshold need translation for home growers.

diseases.name: Mint rust
diseases.evidence: Puccinia menthae. Host-scoped per the roster's whole rust family. Correctly DISTINCT from oregano-rust: host-specialized races (wsu_ext: 'One type infects Native spearmint but not peppermint'). Register the pair.

diseases.name: Verticillium wilt
diseases.evidence: V. dahliae, matches eggplant/strawberry/artichoke. Record carries a LIVE FABRICATED ATTRIBUTION to strike (CAES not in catalog). SEVERITY RAISED medium -> high 2026-09-04, adopting the mint record report's crop-specific reasoning over the orchestrator's provisional default. This is the stand-limiting disease of mint: no cure, soil-persistent as microsclerotia, managed only by site and renewal (uc_ipm ANR 3457). NOTE this deliberately differs from sage's verticillium-wilt at `medium` in the same batch: sage's is a lower-frequency, lower-consequence case, and two crops sharing an id may carry different severities.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.from: SPLIT 1/2 from 'Powdery mildew and anthracnose (leaf spot)'
diseases.evidence: 32 crops. uc_ipm's mint page names powdery mildew for mint. The bundle forced one prevention string across two diseases whose sources disagree on leaf wetness (7406: 'Overhead sprinkling may help reduce powdery mildew').

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.from: SPLIT 2/2 from 'Powdery mildew and anthracnose (leaf spot)'
diseases.evidence: 14 crops. uc_ipm does NOT name anthracnose for mint; the anchor for this limb is usu_ext. SEVERITY RAISED low -> medium 2026-09-04, adopting the mint record report's reasoning: usu_ext's control is rotate plus remove plants plus cut the whole patch to the ground in fall, which is a real cost to the grower, not a cosmetic problem.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.evidence: 59 crops.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.evidence: TYPE CORRECTED insect -> mite. MEASURED: typing a spider mite `insect` makes `sulfur` and `even_watering` ILLEGAL under control_ladder_gate.TYPE_TARGETS.

diseases.name: Root and stem rot
diseases.evidence: Name matches the existing 6-crop umbrella exactly. Taxon unresolved: ncsu_ext names oregano a Phytophthora host, but the shipped Pasco anchor says only 'root rot ... excessive moisture' and never says stem rot.

diseases.name: Mint rust
diseases.evidence: PLA-448 4f RULING: ONE UNPINNED ORGANISM, not an umbrella. Puccinia menthae. T1 anchors already in oregano's vocabulary: psu_ext 'Oregano can be susceptible to fungal diseases such as mint rust and root rot'; rhs 'The fungal disease mint rust can affect oregano'. Display name follows the sources; a bare 'Oregano rust' appears in none.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.from: RENAME from 'Botrytis and humid-weather foliar disease' (Trevor 2026-09-04)
diseases.evidence: The old name led with the ONE organism no source attaches to oregano. VERIFIED: oregano's own shipped uf_ifas anchor publishes exactly two diseases, Powdery Mildew and Root Rot. Botrytis appears in neither.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.evidence: TYPE CORRECTED insect -> mite. SEVERITY medium -> low: every source that ranks rosemary ranks it down ('generally pest and disease free', 'fairly resistant to pests'); no document converts mention-frequency into severity.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.evidence: 59 crops. uc_ipm's rosemary page lists aphids explicitly (unlike its lavender page). Management diverges from whiteflies at both ends of the ladder.

pests.name: Whiteflies
pests.evidence: 5 crops. Sources give whiteflies 'difficult', soap 'reduces but does not eliminate', and an explicit conventional dead end. Bundle origin traced to UGA B1170's 'Aphids; Whiteflies' heading, which attributes susceptibility to germander and monarda and whose rosemary section has no pest content.

pests.name: Spittlebugs
pests.evidence: Philaenus spumarius, shared with lavender and sage. rhs names the binomial and lists 'lavender, rosemary'.

diseases.name: Root and crown rot
diseases.evidence: RULE APPLIED CONSISTENTLY ACROSS THE FIVE-CROP ROT FAMILY: reuse the existing problem-class umbrella whose display name matches, UNLESS the crop's taxon is resolved AND narrower than that umbrella. parsley's `crown-and-root-rot` record defines itself as exactly this umbrella: 'Soilborne water-mold and fungal rots (Pythium, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia)' -- the same genus set in play here. rosemary's taxon is UNRESOLVED AND CONTESTED (uc_ipm links lavender's PRCR document; VCE gives Phytophthora + Pythium; the PNW handbook page indexes Pythium / Berkeleyomyces / Rhizoctonia and NO Phytophthora but returned 403 to every fetch path available and is NOT READ). Unresolved means the umbrella is the honest key. The LADDER must stay genus-agnostic until that page is read.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.evidence: 32 crops. Named on rosemary by ncsu/psu/tamu/umd. Decisively an INDOOR problem (umd: 'usually disappears when the plants are moved further apart or are taken outside in the spring').

pests.name: Spittlebugs
pests.evidence: Shared with lavender and rosemary. Sage's leg is INFERRED not read: rhs names P. spumarius on lavender and rosemary but not sage, and uc_ipm publishes no sage page (404).

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.evidence: 16 crops. sage already types `mite` correctly, unlike oregano/rosemary/thyme.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.evidence: Exact name match to the 11-crop majority id. NOTE both sage sources say 'slugs', neither says 'snails'. LADDER CONSTRAINT MEASURED: the `mollusk` type reaches exactly 8 methods and `airflow_spacing` is NOT one of them, though the record's slug prevention prose leans on airflow.

pests.name: Leafhoppers
pests.evidence: MUST NOT reuse `leafhoppers` (cilantro's aster-yellows/curly-top framing) or `aster-leafhoppers` (parsnip/cosmos vector). Sage's are Eupteryx decemnotata / E. melissae, Lamiaceae specialists and NOT vectors (uc_ipm: 'The Ligurian leafhopper (Eupteryx decemnotata) is a pest of mint, rosemary, sage'; uf_ifas EENY-750). Reusing a vector id would attach a vector ladder to a non-vector pest.

diseases.name: Root and stem rot
diseases.evidence: Name matches the 6-crop umbrella exactly and no admitted document narrows sage's to a genus (Wisconsin D0094 lists Phytophthora/Pythium/Rhizoctonia solani/Fusarium).

diseases.name: Verticillium wilt
diseases.evidence: SEVERITY low -> medium. Defensible on frequency, not consequence: umd 'These fungi remain in the soil for many years ... you must not plant the susceptible plant'; the entry's own text says 'There is no cure.' `low` would make sage the lowest Verticillium record in the dataset (strawberry is medium).

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.evidence: TYPE CORRECTED insect -> mite.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.evidence: 59 crops. Record's mechanism is INVERTED and must be fixed: it says lean soil keeps thyme 'vigorous enough to shrug off aphids'; clemson_hgic says 'Aphids are common in rapidly growing, succulent plants.'

diseases.name: Root and crown rot
diseases.evidence: RULE APPLIED CONSISTENTLY ACROSS THE FIVE-CROP ROT FAMILY: reuse the existing problem-class umbrella whose display name matches, UNLESS the crop's taxon is resolved AND narrower than that umbrella. parsley's `crown-and-root-rot` record defines itself as exactly this umbrella: 'Soilborne water-mold and fungal rots (Pythium, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia)' -- the same genus set in play here. thyme's VCE line ('Thyme (Thymus) - Pythium root rot') is narrower, but it is ONE line in ONE pest-management guide against a record entry whose own name is generic ('Root and crown rot'). That is not enough to mint a one-crop join key. Thyme still does NOT share lavender's id, which was the reviewer's actual finding: lavender is Phytophthora-resolved with a dedicated WSU source.

_retired.name: Generally pest-resistant (aromatic-oil deterrence)
_retired.why: Trevor 2026-09-04. An absence-assertion wearing a pest entry's shape; you cannot ladder controls against 'there are no pests.' A walk of all 128 crops / 912 problem entries found it is the ONLY entry of its kind, so retiring costs no precedent. The sourced absence half (usu_ext 'generally free of pests and diseases WHEN GROWN CORRECTLY'; uwi_hort 'essentially no pest problems IN THE MIDWEST') moves to descriptive prose with its qualifiers restored. The oil-deterrence mechanism is unanchored and refuted and must be corrected in the surviving fields regardless.

_retired.name: Foliar fungal problems in humid weather
_retired.why: Trevor 2026-09-04. A hedge with no organism, no disease and no identifying symptom. The evidence is an INFORMED absence, not a failed hunt: CSU Extension CMG GardenNotes #731 names diseases for eleven herbs and gives Thymus vulgaris exactly one line, 'Do not overwater due to root rot susceptibility.' Corroborated by ncsu (both pages), iastate_ext, uf_ifas Santa Rosa ('no serious pests or diseases are normally seen on the plant'), umd_ext, clemson_hgic's 23-host powdery-mildew list (no herbs) and vce.
